direct_file_reviews.summary: The task requires a pure JavaScript Node.js ESM migration of Python pbkdf2/test2.py into .mjs files in /output, with manual argparse-compatible parsing, no external dependencies, no crypto helper references, and executable-based behavioral observation.
Parallel metadata records actual parallel use with four subagents, successful artifact capture, completed official evaluation, and a failing quality result of 34 passed out of 61.

Parallel status confirms the task identity, native swarm mode, four subagents, artifact files args.mjs, hmac.mjs, test2.mjs, sha1.mjs, pbkdf2.mjs, and completed official evaluation with solution_passed false.
Parallel evaluator summary reports the official RepoZero Py2JS Docker evaluation completed successfully as a process, but the solution failed with 34 of 61 samples passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport stream for the parallel session, accounting for 212 transport events and the completed parent prompt lifecycle.
Parallel session index maps the session id to the workspace session directory used by the main and child actor wire files.
Child agent-0 received the SHA-1 assignment, wrote /output/sha1.mjs, verified known vectors and random SHA-1 checks, and returned a completed SHA-1 handoff.

Child agent-1 received the HMAC-SHA1 assignment, wrote /output/hmac.mjs, found only hmac.mjs present during an in-place dependency check, verified by scratch copy, and returned a completed HMAC handoff.
Child agent-2 received the PBKDF2 assignment, wrote /output/pbkdf2.mjs, hit ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND for /output/sha1.mjs during verification, then verified in a temporary copied workspace.
Child agent-3 received the CLI/parser assignment, wrote /output/args.mjs and /output/test2.mjs, observed module-load failures because sha1.mjs was absent, then verified parser and wiring with a stub.

Parallel parent probed the executable, delegated four module scopes through AgentSwarm, received all handoffs, ran sample and edge regressions, patched args.mjs and hmac.mjs, and ended with a successful self-report.

direct_file_reviews.summary: The serial run received the same PBKDF2 migration prompt and the same ESM, no-dependency, CLI parity, and /output delivery requirements as the parallel run.
Serial metadata records no parallel use, no subagents, successful artifact capture, completed official evaluation, and a failing quality result of 38 passed out of 61.
Serial status confirms task identity, no delegation, artifact files test2.mjs plus lib modules, and completed official evaluation with solution_passed false.
Serial evaluator summary reports the official RepoZero Py2JS Docker evaluation completed successfully as a process, but the solution failed with 38 of 61 samples passing.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server transport stream for the serial session, accounting for 44 transport events and the completed single-parent prompt lifecycle.
Serial session index maps the session id to the single main actor wire file and workspace directory.
Serial main actor probed executable behavior, wrote all SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, bytes, argparse, and entry modules in one step, then ran sample, random, and error-path checks before final response.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized ESM .mjs output, no external dependencies, no crypto helper references, manual CLI parsing, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior, UTF-8 handling, and output under /output.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After three executable probes, the parent delegated four owned scopes: SHA-1, HMAC-SHA1, PBKDF2, and CLI/entry wiring. The parent retained integration and final verification responsibility.
parallel.implementation: Children created top-level /output/sha1.mjs, /output/hmac.mjs, /output/pbkdf2.mjs, /output/args.mjs, and /output/test2.mjs using fixed imports and exports. The parent later patched argparse edge behavior and removed a forbidden comment mention.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final artifact contains five top-level .mjs files. Integration succeeded enough for sample cases, edge checks, syntax checks, grep checks, and 30 random executable comparisons run by the parent.
parallel.verification: Verification included executable probes before delegation, child-local vector checks, parent sample comparisons, edge-case comparisons, fixed-case reruns, fuzz comparisons, syntax checking, and a final sample after the hmac comment edit.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 34/61 despite local checks. The visible process also had transient broken /output states while children tested before dependent sibling modules existed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the same ESM .mjs, no-dependency, CLI parity, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1, executable-observation, and /output delivery requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery without child delegation or handoff boundaries.
serial.implementation: The serial actor wrote /output/test2.mjs plus lib/sha1.mjs, lib/hmac.mjs, lib/pbkdf2.mjs, lib/bytes.mjs, and lib/argparse.mjs in one coherent tree, with test2.mjs importing from lib modules.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All modules were written before the serial actor ran integrated sample and random tests; artifact capture later recorded the expected entry and supporting lib files.
serial.verification: Serial verification compared all four sample cases, ran 15 random executable differentials, and checked basic success and error paths, but did not later correct all argparse edge behavior seen in the parallel run.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Official evaluation still failed at 38/61. The serial final parser visibly used test2.mjs as the usage program name and strict digit-only integer parsing, leaving some CLI parity gaps.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the required pure ESM, .mjs, no-dependency, manual CLI, executable-observation, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and acted on the same migration requirements, including .mjs modules, manual parsing, /output placement, and no external modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition gap is visible at the prompt level; later differences are in execution strategy and edge-case implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split the work across four children for SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, and CLI/entry modules, with the parent later integrating and checking.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all implementation and verification in the main actor and wrote the full file set in one implementation step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced child handoffs and interdependent shared-file timing; serial avoided those boundaries but had less independent specialization.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent gave fixed top-level module signatures and import paths to all children, so interfaces were explicit, but dependencies were exposed live in the same /output directory.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created its own lib module namespace and imports in one context, so no child had to depend on a sibling file before it existed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel interface contract was adequate, but the live shared workspace exposed incomplete dependency state during child verification; serial had no such handoff or shared-state boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced flat modules named args.mjs, hmac.mjs, pbkdf2.mjs, sha1.mjs, and test2.mjs, then patched parser and comment issues after integrated edge checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a lib-based implementation with sha1, hmac, pbkdf2, bytes, argparse, and test2 entry files in one pass.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implemented standard PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 and passed visible sample/random checks; parallel made additional argparse corrections that serial did not, while serial kept a simpler module tree.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All four children completed and returned handoffs; the parent joined them through AgentSwarm result, then performed follow-up tests and edits.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: There were no child results; the serial actor directly owned the implementation lifecycle and moved from writing to verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel required child-result collection and parent takeover of integration issues, while serial had no retrieval or child-result lifecycle risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote directly into shared /output; HMAC and PBKDF2/CLI checks observed missing sibling dependencies before the output tree was complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the complete module tree in one step and then executed integrated tests without missing-module failures.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material coordination difference: parallel's live shared tree caused transient broken integration states; serial avoided them by single-owner sequencing.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran four samples, edge cases, fixed-case reruns, 30 fuzz comparisons, syntax checks, and grep checks, then had an official 34/61 failing evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran four samples, 15 random comparisons, and basic error-path checks, then had an official 38/61 failing evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel performed broader self-verification and fixed more visible parser parity issues, but the official hidden evaluation still scored it lower than serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents, 41 LLM requests, 43 tool calls, about 400 agent seconds, and closed after parent integration checks.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor, 5 LLM requests, 12 tool calls, about 122 agent seconds, and closed after sample/random checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent much more budget on coordination and repeated verification, but did not time out; serial was shorter and simpler.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed. The serial run scored 38/61 and the parallel run scored 34/61, so there is a quality gap but not a discordant pass/fail outcome. The concrete trajectory difference is that parallel decomposed into four interdependent children sharing /output, causing temporary missing-module verification failures and later parent integration fixes, while serial wrote and tested one coherent tree directly. The official records available here do not expose individual hidden failing samples, so the process evidence supports a parallel adverse coordination cost but not an exclusive causal explanation for the 4-case score gap.
parallel_contributors: The parent split interdependent modules across four children and let them write directly to /output, so children testing before all siblings landed saw missing modules.
The parent later patched parser edge cases and removed a forbidden comment mention, showing extra integration/rework after child handoff.
serial_contributors: The serial actor wrote all modules in one pass and ran integrated sample/random tests without child dependency timing failures.
The serial parser remained less faithful on some observed CLI edges, including usage program naming and strict integer parsing.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used top-level sibling modules and TextEncoder; serial used a lib directory, a bytes helper, and custom UTF-8 encoding.
Serial reported usage as test2.mjs on error paths, while the executable's usage string was test2_executable.
Both runs implemented standard PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1 and passed visible samples/random probes, yet hidden official tests still failed.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluation summaries expose only aggregate pass counts, not per-case hidden failure reasons.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: parallel adverse coordination episode observed, but no discordant outcome and no exclusive root cause for the score gap

candidates.reason: Parallel had explicit implementation owners for SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, and CLI files, and each owner wrote code.
The parent explicitly retained integration and verification after receiving child outputs, so integration was not unowned.
The entry file and final /output artifact were produced and captured; assembly was owned by the CLI child and parent.
The parent drove probing, delegation, child result collection, patching, regression checks, and final delivery.
The parent ran a short executable preflight before delegation, but it did not block productive implementation long enough to create unfinished work or a shortened closure window.
There was no separate investigator phase; the parent performed limited behavior probes and then launched implementation children.
No indispensable implementation path was left without capacity; all delegated modules completed and the parent had time for integration checks.
The four-child fan-out increased time and tool use but the run completed, all children returned, and there is no direct budget-exhaustion terminal state.
No one child received an overbroad task that it could not checkpoint; each child scope was a single module or the CLI pair and all returned.

The child briefs included the task constraints, output paths, module interfaces, and relevant parser obligations; the later parser correction was a parent-discovered behavior edge, not an omitted already-known child requirement.
The parent supplied concrete file names, import paths, function names, argument types, and return types for the interdependent modules.
No known finding is shown disappearing through transfer; the parent received child summaries and acted on the artifacts.
The AgentSwarm result was large, but the parent consumed it enough to run integrated tests, diagnose parser diffs, and patch files.
No child or parent action is shown relying on a handoff that described superseded workspace state; the dependency failures happened before sibling files existed.
The handoffs do not present unresolved incompatible contracts or claims; the fixed module interfaces remained consistent.

The parent did make a completion statement, but it also ran integrated samples, edge checks, fuzz checks, syntax checks, and grep checks; the official hidden failure alone cannot establish a parent-visible unresolved acceptance gap.
There was no replacement child or retry assignment that repeated prior work without inherited checkpoints.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No active child was explicitly cancelled, stopped, or interrupted before returning a needed result.
The final candidate files were present and integrated before closure; no complete candidate was merely left unpromoted or unplaced until too late.
The only visible post-regression edit was a comment-only removal of a forbidden mention in hmac.mjs, followed by a cleanliness check and sample run; it was not a late implementation merge.
All completed child implementation files were present in /output, exercised by the parent, and included in artifact validation.
There was no separate verifier child with a concrete finding trapped below the parent; verification was either child-local or parent-run.
The parent did take over integration after child-level module-load failures, ran end-to-end tests, and patched visible parser and comment issues before closure.
The parent received the AgentSwarm result and then used the created files in integrated tests and targeted edits; no completed child result is shown ignored.
The parent did not wait until timeout without inspection; it actively ran probes, integration checks, parser checks, grep, and a final sample.
Although several files were written in parallel, their responsibilities were complementary SHA-1, HMAC, PBKDF2, and CLI modules rather than competing cross-file implementations of the same behavior.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source file and observing or reconciling one another's concurrent same-file changes.
No non-entry source produced by one live agent was deleted, recreated, or wholesale rewritten by another actor.
The entry file was written by the CLI child and not replaced by another live owner; later parent edits affected args.mjs and an hmac comment.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs or invalidated another actor's final-tree work.

The parent launched multiple children to write interdependent top-level files directly into /output; while that tree was partial, children observed missing sibling dependencies and had to abandon in-place verification for scratch copies or stubs. Serial avoided this by writing and then testing one coherent tree.
candidates.realized_consequence: Child-level in-place verification was invalidated by missing sibling modules, forcing scratch/stub verification and parent re-integration checks before delivery.
candidates.near_match_reason: The child modules were complementary and contract-compatible, not competing implementations of the same behavior; the problem was the live shared output tree's incomplete state.

candidates.reason: No child-created cache, temporary artifact, fixture, or process was consumed by another actor as a stable reference environment; scratch directories were used only locally for verification and cleaned up.

retained_patterns.reason: Multiple children wrote interdependent files straight into the same /output tree, and child-level validation observed that tree while incomplete. Agent-1 saw only hmac.mjs, agent-2 and agent-3 hit missing sha1.mjs import failures, and parent verification had to become the real integration boundary. Corrective boundary: stage child work in isolated directories or delay dependent integration checks until all promised sibling files are present.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Child-level in-place verification was invalidated by missing sibling modules, forcing scratch/stub verification and parent re-integration checks before delivery.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The child modules were complementary and contract-compatible, not competing implementations of the same behavior; the problem was the live shared output tree's incomplete state.

deduplicated_same_label_episodes: The agent-1, agent-2, and agent-3 missing-dependency observations are treated as one shared-output partial-state episode, not three separate labels.
suppressed_same_chain_candidates: No Failure Takeover rejected because the parent later integrated and retested after child-level failures.
Missing Implementation Join rejected because all child outputs were ultimately present and used.
Cross-File Scope Collision rejected because no competing file-scope design conflict was present.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the shared workspace write episode had a direct adverse parallel coordination consequence.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The dependency failures, scratch verification, and parent rechecks are one propagation chain, so only Unisolated Workspace Writes is retained for that episode.
